actions.do: Contain it. If the samples confirm a problem, close the valves either side of pipe 229 so the water stops moving on from it.

guidance.quote: Operational responses to consider include complete isolation of the affected area or reducing or diverting flow (e.g., opening/closing valves, flushing, isolating tanks, or changing the hydraulic gradient in the system through pump and tank operations) to slow or limit the spread.

actions.do: Flush downstream of the segment once it is isolated, working outward from clean water, and retest before putting it back in service.

guidance.quote: This minimizes the spread of sediment to other parts of the system and produces a higher velocity of flow. • Spot flushing is used to remove stagnant water from low water use areas such as dead-end water mains. Spot flushing can be performed on a regular schedule at areas with known problems (e.g., a history of customer complaints) or can be performed when needed (e.g., based on water quality parameters).
guidance.source: Distribution System Water Quality: Protecting Water Quality Through Distribution System Flushing, US EPA, Office of Water, 2022, p. 1

actions.do: Inspect pipe 229 itself (cast iron, laid in 1945, 610 mm across, 1 recorded break; these attributes are synthetic). If it is opened or repaired, disinfect and test it before it goes back in service.

guidance.quote: 4.4 Trench Work As described previously, trench water has a high potential for contaminating water mains during installation and repair. Dewatering the trench to a level below the pipe invert may be necessary to avoid contamination. Pierson et al (2001) suggest using submersible pumps and fittings used for clean water work only to avoid cross-contamination from sewage water applications.
guidance.source: New or Repaired Water Mains (distribution system issue paper), AWWA, with Economic and Engineering Services, Inc, for US EPA, 2002, p. 11

actions.do: Tell the people downstream what is known, what is not, and when they will hear more.

scenarios.notice: Sensors in part of the water network picked up a change in water quality, first at node 203. Samples are being taken to find out what changed, and this notice will be updated when their results are in. Clarity reads only pH, dissolved solids and transparency. It cannot detect lead, bacteria or any specific contaminant.
caveats: This is a simulation. The network is WNTR's Net3 example (EPANET example network 3), the event was injected by the simulation, and no real sensor or pipe is involved.

The four events here were chosen by hand. Run for a change entering at every pipe in turn: 30 of the 117 pipes reach no sensor within six hours, so a change there goes unseen. Of the rest, when two or more sensors alert (71 pipes) the true pipe is ranked first for 32 and in the top three for 56; when only one alerts (16 pipes), first for 4.
Flow directions and travel times are frozen at one hour of the simulated day. In a real network they change with demand, so a trace has to use the hour the event happened.
Pipe material, age and break history are synthetic, and the risk score built from them is set by hand, not learned from failures.
Travel time assumes the change moves with the water and does not spread, mix or decay on the way.
The downstream count is junctions and their simulated demand, a stand-in for people served. It is not a customer count.
scenarios.check: The simulation put the change in pipe 229. The trace ranked it number 1 of 24, with 41% of the weight.
